title: Per-cell sqlite3_column_value reuse in write_json_to_buf
impact: Hoists `sqlite3_column_value(stmt, i)` once per cell inside `write_json_to_buf` and dispatches through `sqlite3_value_type` / `sqlite3_value_int64` / `sqlite3_value_double` / `sqlite3_value_text` / `sqlite3_value_bytes` / `sqlite3_value_blob` instead of repeating `sqlite3_column_*`. The SQLite amalgamation defines `sqlite3_column_*` as `sqlite3_value_* ∘ columnMem`, so each per-cell access currently runs a fresh `columnMem` lookup (mutex enter/leave + result-row range check, no-op on SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX connections but still function calls) plus `columnMallocFailure` (`sqlite3ApiExit`). Hoisting collapses 2-3 `columnMem` calls per cell into 1; output is bit-identical. Safe because resqlite opens every connection with `SQLITE_OPEN_NOMUTEX` and dedicates each connection to one isolate worker, so the SQLite `unprotected sqlite3_value` multithread warning does not apply. Two order-flipped focused passes reproduce same-direction wins: `select_bytes_int_heavy.dart` **−0.9 % to −4.7 %** on integer lanes, `select_bytes_real_int_fastpath.dart` **−3.1 % to −6.1 %** on integral-REAL lanes (fractional-REAL guard inside ±1 %, confirming the saving is FFI-lookup-shaped and not noise — `snprintf("%.17g")` dominates that lane), `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` **−1.3 % to −6.1 %** on int / mixed wide lanes, `large_bytes_transfer.dart` **−2.0 % to −3.8 %** on the large/small TEXT lanes. ~10 net additional lines of C; no public API change.
